chunks: 5403 - Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir عليه السلام, who said:
"Indeed, the name of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله in the scriptures of Ibrahim is al-Mahi, in the Torah of Musa al-Hadd, in the Gospel of Isa Ahmad, and in the Furqan Muhammad."

It was said: "What is the interpretation of al-Mahi?" He said: "Al-Mahi [is the eraser of] the form of idols, the remover of idols and divining arrows, and of every object worshipped besides al-Rahman."
And it was said: "What is the interpretation of al-Hadd?" He said: "He opposes whoever opposes Allah and His religion, whether near or far."

It was said: "What is the interpretation of Ahmad?" He said: "The praise of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for him in the scriptures is beautiful, because of the praiseworthy deeds for which he was praised."

It was said: "What is the interpretation of Muhammad?" He said: "Indeed Allah, His angels, all His Prophets, His Messengers, and all their communities praise him and send blessings upon him, and indeed his name written upon the Throne is: Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.

And he عليه السلام used to wear Yemeni caps, white caps, and striped headgear with two flaps in wars. He had a short spear upon which he would lean, and he would bring it out on the two Eids and deliver the sermon with it. He had a rod called al-Mamshuq, a tent called al-Kinn, a bowl called al-Sa'ah, and a drinking vessel called al-Riyy. He had two horses, one called al-Murtajiz and the other al-Sakb; two mules, one called al-Duldul and the other al-Shahba'; two she-camels, one called al-'Adhba' and the other al-Jad'a'; two swords, one called Dhu al-Faqar and the other al-'Awn; and two other swords, one called al-Mikhdham and the other al-Rasum. He had a donkey called al-Ya'fur, a turban called al-Sahab, a coat of armor called Dhat al-Fudul with three silver rings, one in front of it and two behind it, a banner called al-'Uqab, a camel used for carrying loads called al-Dibaj, a standard called al-Ma'lum, and a helmet called al-As'ad.

So he delivered all of that to Ali عليه السلام at the time of his death, and he took out his ring and placed it on his finger. Then Ali عليه السلام mentioned that he found in the hilt of one of his swords a sheet containing three phrases: "Maintain ties with one who cuts you off; speak the truth even against yourself; and do good to one who has wronged you."

key_terms.الْحَادُّ: the one who opposes those who oppose Allah and His religion
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne, upon which the Prophet’s name is said to be written
key_terms.الْفُرْقَانِ: the Qur'an, described here as containing the name Muhammad
key_terms.الْمَاحِي: the one who effaces idols and false objects of worship
key_terms.ذُو الْفَقَارِ: the named sword among the Prophet’s weapons
key_terms.صُحُفِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: the scriptures of Ibrahim in which one of the Prophet’s names is mentioned
key_terms.صِلْ مَنْ قَطَعَكَ: maintain ties with one who severs ties with you

ai.seo_question: What do the names al-Mahi, al-Hadd, Ahmad, and Muhammad mean in Shia hadith, and what did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم leave to Imam Ali عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains several names of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as they appear in earlier revealed scriptures, showing his divinely recognized status across prophetic history. It also records some of his personal belongings and concludes with ethical instructions transmitted to Imam Ali عليه السلام, linking Prophetic legacy with moral conduct and succession.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5403 - Yunus ibn Abd Al-Rahman narrated from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:

"Indeed, the name of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) in the scriptures of Ibrahim is Al-Mahi (the Eraser), in the Torah of Musa it is Al-Had (the Opponent), in the Gospel of Isa it is Ahmad, and in the Qur'an it is Muhammad (sw)."

It was asked: "What is the meaning of Al-Mahi?"
Imam (as) said: "Al-Mahi is "The one who erases the image of idols, removes the traces of false deities, and eliminates every object of worship besides the Most Merciful (swt)."

It was asked: "What is the meaning of Al-Had?"
Imam (as) said: "Al-Had is the one who stands in opposition to those who oppose Allah (swt) and His (swt) religion, whether they are near or far."

It was asked: "What is the meaning of Ahmad?"
Imam (as) said: "Ahmad means that Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has praised him in the scriptures for the praiseworthy deeds he performed."

It was asked: "What is the meaning of Muhammad?"
Imam (as) said: "Indeed, Allah (swt), His (swt) angels, all His (swt) Prophets (as), Messengers (as), and all their praise and send blessings upon Him (sw), and His (sw) name is inscribed upon the Throne: 'Muhammad (sw) is the Messenger of Allah (swt).'"

He (sw) used to wear Yemeni caps, white caps, and a wrapped turban with two flaps during battles.
He (sw) had a staff called 'Anazah, which he would lean on and take out for the two Eid sermons.
He (sw) had a rod called Al-Mamshuq and a tent called Al-Kinn.
He (sw) had a large wooden bowl called Al-Sa'ah and a drinking vessel called Al-Riyy.
He (sw) had two horses: one named Al-Murtajiz and the other named Al-Sakb.
He (sw) had two mules: one named Al-Duldul and the other named Al-Shahba.
He (sw) had two camels: one named Al-'Adhba and the other named Al-Jad'a.
He (sw) had two swords: one named Dhu Al-Fiqar and the other named Al-'Awn.
He (sw) had two additional swords: one named Al-Mikhdham and the other named Al-Rasum.
He (sw) had a donkey named Al-Ya'fur.
He (sw) had a turban called Al-Sahab.
He (sw) had a coat of armor called Dhat Al-Fudul, which had three silver rings - one in the front and two in the back.
He (sw) had a banner called Al-'Uqab.
He (sw) had a camel for carrying loads named Al-Dibaj.
He (sw) had a flag called Al-Ma'lum.
He (sw) had a war helmet called Al-As'ad.

Upon His (sw)  passing, He (sw) entrusted all of these to Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), and placed his ring on Imam Ali's (as) finger.
Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said that he found a scroll inside the hilt of one of the Prophet's (sw) swords, which contained three statements:
"Maintain ties with those who cut you off."
"Speak the truth, even if it is against yourself."
"Show kindness to those who wrong you."
